text.p: Estonian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Central Bank will issue new 500-kroon bank notes in early 1997. The overall design will remain unchanged, but security elements will be improved. The old type bank notes will also stay in circulation.

- The Estonian Small Business Association (EVEA) presented its business support awards for 1996. The annual award went to Innterior Minister Riivo Sinijarv, for his efforts as first chairman of EVEA and his achievements in European integration as the European affairs minister.
- Police in Tallinn received a new control centre, the most technically advanced in Estonia, worth 1.2 million kroons.
- All fuel companies will increase prices after the increase of fuel excise from January 1.
- Two private companies have been contracted to arrange a New Year fireworks in the centre of Tallin, with the estimated cost of 100,000 kroons.
- Estonia's economic growth in 1996 is estimated at 2.5-2.9 percent. CPI growth is calculated to be 14.3 percent and the inflation rate is 25 percent.
